editorial-max-width.role: Maximum width of the desktop editorial grid; it centres above the 2560 px controlled-growth cap

section-gap.role: Vertical spacing between major editorial blocks

home-hero-content-padding-block-end.role: Bottom inset below the three-line title in the home capella hero

home-first-screen-panel-height.role: Desktop height of each home hero panel so its panels, one-row advantage cards and their outer 24 px insets fit in the viewport

shadows.status: No owned shadow token was found in the inspected Figma variables

motion.reduced-motion: Disable the Home Hero reveal and the Home teacher CTA arrow transition when prefers-reduced-motion is reduce; keep both in their final/default positions immediately.
motion.home-other-decorative-motion: disabled except for the approved Home teacher CTA hover feedback

hover-opacity.role: Pointer hover feedback where Figma uses opacity

focus-ring-offset.role: Separates focus outline from control surface

usage_rules: Use a real button for actions and a real link for navigation
Do not invent one-off colors or radii
do_not: Do not nest links inside buttons
Do not remove visible focus treatment

state_contract.hover: Primary uses interaction.hover-opacity while preserving exactly the default geometry and padding; secondary and icon controls use neutral-100/muted surfaces as shown in Figma. Text variants without the close icon keep 1.5rem (24px) end padding in every state. Play transitions size with duration-button-play-hover (800ms) and easing-out; arrows transition background with duration-micro and easing-out.
state_contract.focus-visible: Brand outline uses interaction focus ring width and offset and remains a real keyboard behavior, but is not duplicated as an artificial Storybook specimen.
state_contract.active: Use interaction.active-opacity and preserve Primary geometry during real pointer hover.
state_contract.disabled: Use native disabled for buttons or aria-disabled without href for links, interaction.disabled-opacity, and suppress hover/active.
state_contract.loading: Button-only state: set disabled and aria-busy, replace visible label, hide optional icon, and do not add motion before motion tokens exist.

semantics.icon-only: Requires a non-empty accessible label; SVGs are decorative.

Button.responsive: Keep the 4rem base control size and at least 44px target in desktop, tablet and mobile. Component-specific tablet/mobile refinements belong to stage 6; no Button breakpoint is introduced in stage 3.

checks: stable Primary geometry on real hover

usage_rules: Use for compact metadata or a non-editable category marker
Use inverse only over imagery or inverse surfaces; its border and text use colors.surface
do_not: Do not use badges as buttons unless they expose button semantics and states

usage_rules: Preserve link semantics and visited-state policy where useful
On hover, roll the duplicated label upward through its clipped one-line track over 400 ms with the standard CSS ease curve
do_not: Do not use a span with click handler for navigation

usage_rules: Category determines the icon
The whole card may be clickable only with valid accessible link markup
The title uses Heading/H3 at weight 500
Hover and focus-within change the title color immediately
do_not: Do not add decorative nested cards

usage_rules: Use only for the approved factual metrics on the home page
Keep the card 170px high with 24px top and inline padding and 16px bottom padding; align the value to the top and the secondary label to the bottom
Use colors.text-secondary-on-muted for the label so secondary text passes WCAG AA on the muted card surface
do_not: Do not turn ordinary copy into dashboard-like statistics

usage_rules: Every input has a persistent programmatic label
Errors are associated with the field and announced
Default uses a 20px label; typing and filled use a 14px secondary label above the 20px value
The label uses colors.text-secondary-on-muted in every state so secondary text passes WCAG AA on the muted field surface
The 64px control uses 16px inline and 2px block padding; stacked label and value line boxes are contiguous and vertically centered
Focus uses the single 1px brand border shown by the Figma typing state; do not add a second outer outline
The date variant renders as a numeric DD.MM.YYYY mask in a text input, has no native calendar affordance, and corrects a complete invalid value to the nearest valid date no later than today
The telephone variant accepts typed or pasted digits only and formats them as the Russian +7 (999) 999-99-99 mask
do_not: Do not use placeholder as the only label
Do not expose the native date-picker calendar or allow free-form telephone characters

usage_rules: Use semantic table markup when relationships are tabular
Provide a deliberate mobile representation without losing labels
Every data row, including the final row, ends with a 1px color-border-subtle stroke; page wrappers must not duplicate this border
do_not: Do not hide essential columns only to fit mobile

usage_rules: Use native details and summary disclosure semantics
Use the Figma plus and minus assets with a 2px stroke
Hover changes title, meta and icon to colors.text-secondary immediately
Open and close use native details disclosure without animation
Preserve image aspect ratio per variant
Show provider and media type without relying on color alone
Big and small variants are both 540px high on desktop
Small keeps 16px between image and title and aligns metadata badges to the bottom
Big uses inverse Badge over imagery
Big and small titles use their Figma heading roles at weight 500
Show the decorative Play marker only for the video media type in either card size: 24px from the left/top in Big and 24px from the left plus 16px from the top inside Small imagery
The video-card link opens the external provider URL in a separate tab; Play does not create a separate action
Derive the visible provider tag from the URL for YouTube, RuTube and VK Video
do_not: Do not expose Play as a nested interactive control or prevent the card link from opening the external video
Do not use low-resolution source images

usage_rules: Submit once per idempotency token
Explain privacy processing before submission and link to the approved privacy policy route
Use the same 500px-wide visual contract for home and about; page composition owns placement
Default and submitting are at least 536px high; success is at least 456px high
Compose the four required fields from Input and the action from Button
Submitting preserves values and disables repeat submission without hiding the fields
Validation errors preserve entered values and are communicated only by their associated Input errors; network and server errors use the form error with role=alert
Keep the native POST form usable without JavaScript and let orlyata-core inject nonce and idempotency fields through the documented hook
Use application-success.svg from Figma for the success state
do_not: Do not send field values to analytics
Do not erase entered values on recoverable failure

usage_rules: Desktop rail owns the primary navigation and admission CTA
Desktop geometry is 250 px wide with the 240 x 110 px logo at 12 px from the top, navigation at 152 px and CTA at 24 px from the bottom of the sidebar viewport
Navigation uses a semantic nav/list/link structure and aria-current=page for the current route
On internal pages, hovering the logo changes only its opacity to 90%; the home-page Sidebar suppresses this hover treatment
The muted surface of a current navigation item starts 8 px from the left edge of the link; the label keeps the shared navigation padding
The rail is not rendered below the desktop breakpoint until separate tablet and mobile navigation is approved
do_not: Do not preserve the desktop rail on mobile by shrinking it
Do not turn the admission CTA or navigation links into JavaScript-only controls

usage_rules: Contacts are sourced from site settings
Navigation mirrors real routes
Desktop reference geometry is 1616 by 469 px with 48 px padding and a 24 px radius
The required legal destination is the privacy policy route from the approved sitemap
Secondary text on the inverse surface uses the WCAG AA alias #9999a2 instead of the failing Figma value #71717a
The desktop Footer is not displayed below 1280 px until the separate tablet and mobile layouts are approved
do_not: Do not duplicate editable contact values in templates

HomeDesktopPreview.viewport: desktop only (1280–2560+); exact comparison target 1920 px
implementation_rules: The 1900 px Figma frame is normalized to the 1920 px desktop target without changing the internal 1617 px editorial canvas relationship.
A persistent 250 px Sidebar occupies the left rail; the editorial canvas starts at the normalized equivalent of the Figma 261 px offset.

The hero consists of two rounded panels separated by 16 px: the capella panel automatically plays the supplied muted, looping, inline vertical hero-preview.mp4 with object-fit: cover, while the news panel remains green.

The capella preview video is covered by linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.00) 63.53%, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.80) 100%). Its Play control and the three-line title «Хоровая / капелла / мальчиков» stay above the gradient.

The capella title uses the full available content width without clipping and has a 32 px bottom inset. The news panel uses the supplied bg-news.png as its own full-size image layer with object-fit: cover, matching the Figma image layer and Fill behaviour.
The Play link remains a no-JavaScript fallback to hero-original.mp4. With JavaScript it opens a native dialog and starts the original video only after the explicit click.

Home motion is limited to the Hero page-load effect and the teacher CTA hover feedback: the three masked hero-title lines move from translateY(130%) to their final position over 1600 ms with easeOutQuint and delays of 70, 140 and 210 ms, matching the inspected AnimatedText2 implementation on oxem.ru. The green teacher CTA shifts only its white arrow right by Space 2 (8 px) on pointer hover, using duration-micro and easing-out, and returns it to its default position when the pointer leaves. All other decorative animations and transitions on the Home page are disabled. The title is server-rendered and readable without JavaScript; prefers-reduced-motion shows the final state immediately and keeps the CTA arrow stationary.
The four Advantage cards use their existing 170 px contract and appear beneath the hero in one desktop row.
Media gallery, history, application CTA and achievements are page sections, not new universal components; each reuses an owned component where a contract exists.

The history section follows Figma 4641:3419: its desktop box is 1617 by 544 px including the 1px top stroke and Heading/H2; its left Lead is paired with the tags «о капелле» and «педагоги», while its right column contains Body copy and two 100 px circular teacher frames followed by a 100 px green teacher CTA.

The application CTA follows Figma 4641:3437: Heading/Lead 64 «Хотите вырастить творческую личность — запишите мальчика в капеллу» is centered above the 1617 by 620 px atmospheric container. The existing ApplicationForm is centered in that container; do not add supporting marketing copy that is absent from the Figma node.
The application CTA is the only other approved page context for the atmospheric green-to-dark treatment; it uses authentic Figma imagery, the existing ApplicationForm and the approved privacy link.
The achievements preview uses the existing semantic DataTable with Year, Achievement, Choir and Competition columns.
Preview text, labels and CTA names are copied exactly from their approved Figma node or project content source; implementation must not invent or paraphrase copy.
Stage 5.1 uses controlled preview fixtures for CMS-owned news, media and achievements. Those fixtures must be removed when stage 5.2 connects CMS queries.
assets: Figma images from 4641:3330 are copied locally into theme assets; the two teacher circles use the supplied local exports Frame 4216.png and Frame 4240.png. The supplied hero videos preview.mp4 and original.mp4 are stored as assets/videos/home/hero-preview.mp4 and hero-original.mp4; the supplied bg-news.png is assets/images/home/news-background.png and bg-form.png is assets/images/home/application-background.png. Remote short-lived MCP URLs are never used in production markup.
gaps: tablet and mobile composition belongs to stage 6

layout.grid: Every page uses an editorial content canvas with a minimum 24 px (Space 5) inline gutter from the left navigation rail and from the browser edge. On desktop the canvas is a four-column equal grid with 16 px (Space 4) gaps. Tablet and mobile may recompose the number of columns, but retain the 24 px outer gutter.
layout.page_width: The desktop design target is a 1920 px viewport. Inspected 1900 px Figma frames are normalized to 1920 during implementation. Reviewed fluid values continue scaling to 2560 px; beyond 2560 px the composition is centred.
layout.section_rhythm: Major editorial blocks are separated by 120 px (layout.section-gap); internal component and subsection spacing continues to use its own approved token. Use whitespace, rules and surface changes rather than repeated card containers.
layout.density: Spacious marketing sections with denser data tables for news, scores and achievements.
responsive_rules: Use exactly three global layout modes: mobile 320–767, tablet 768–1279, desktop 1280–2560+.
Keep html font-size at 100%; do not implement global viewport scaling through the root font size.
Use rem for type, spacing, component size and radius. Use vw only as the fluid term of reviewed clamp() tokens.
Media queries use px and 1px is allowed for hairline borders.
Components may recompose at 1280 and 768; mobile is not a uniformly shrunken desktop.
Do not add global breakpoints without updating this manifest first.
Support 320 px without horizontal page scrolling and without clipping text.
Between 1920 and 2560 px, reviewed fluid values may continue growing. Above 2560 px, full-bleed backgrounds may extend but content and typography do not continue growing.

rules: Stories import the production entrypoint and must not duplicate production tokens or component styles.
Story-only CSS may arrange and label specimens but may not redefine visual token values.
Accessibility checks fail on violations; local Playwright screenshots are the visual baseline and do not require a cloud service.

Every production component story provides a typed Playground with args and argTypes for meaningful public properties; static Variants and States remain deterministic visual baselines with Controls disabled.
Every production-component change updates its Storybook story and relevant checks, then rebuilds the published staging Storybook before completion.
storybook.font_validation: Playwright waits for the F37 Ginger Cyrillic VF FontFace to reach loaded status before axe or screenshot assertions.

visual_language.mood: Warm, confident and contemporary editorial identity: youthful without childish decoration, institutional without bureaucracy.
composition_rules: Use the green brand accent sparingly against white and near-black surfaces.
Use large photography and typographic hierarchy as primary visual devices.
Use a soft green-to-dark atmospheric gradient only in approved hero and application contexts.
Keep data-heavy sections flat, aligned and readable; use rules rather than nested cards.
Preserve generous whitespace between major sections.
imagery_rules: Prioritise authentic photographs of the choir, performances, teachers and community.
Never distort or arbitrarily crop faces; define focal points where supported.
Use approved aspect ratios per MediaCard variant and responsive mode.
Do not upscale weak migration assets without review.
iconography_rules: Use the existing simple monochrome icon language and the approved category mapping.
Social icons may be editor-managed SVG only after sanitisation.
Icons supplement labels and must not be the only accessible name.
motion_rules: Only the approved Home Hero title reveal and Home teacher CTA arrow hover feedback may animate.
The muted looping Home Hero preview is the only approved autoplay media; do not add other autoplay media or continuous ornamental motion.
anti_patterns: Unowned accent colors or new gradients
Arbitrary type sizes or spacing outside tokens
Desktop scaled down uniformly for mobile

accessibility.contrast_policy: Target WCAG 2.2 AA for text and meaningful controls. Validate the green/white and secondary-text combinations before release.
accessibility.keyboard_policy: All navigation, filters, accordions, galleries and forms must work by keyboard in a logical DOM order.
accessibility.focus_policy: Every interactive element has a visible :focus-visible style not dependent on hover. Focus styling is a required design-system gap to resolve.
accessibility.reduced_motion_policy: Disable the approved Home Hero title reveal and teacher CTA arrow hover transition under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

governance.token_policy: Use semantic CSS custom properties backed by this manifest. Raw values are allowed only while defining a token, not at call sites.
governance.component_policy: Reuse an owned component before creating a local variant. Every interactive component ships with all applicable states and responsive behaviour.
governance.when_to_add_new_tokens: Add a token when a new semantic role is approved or a value repeats across at least two owned components. Document source and intended role.
governance.when_to_add_new_components: Add a component for repeated structure or behaviour with a stable API. One-off page composition remains a section, not a universal component.

open_questions: Design and approve tablet and mobile typography, layout, navigation and all component variants.
Audit hard-coded Figma spacing values and complete the spacing scale before implementation.
Design focus-visible, active, disabled, loading and error states missing from the component boards.
Confirm the legal consent control and copy for the application form.
Confirm the category icon mapping for news, announcements and achievements.
Review color contrast for green with white text, secondary text and thin borders.
